security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel capability-bounds validation code computes the top bound via saturating GCBASE+GCLEN addition on hardware that implements Zytopr, or vice versa uses GCTOP on hardware lacking Zytopr, causing two code paths to derive inconsistent top values for the same capability when the capability's architectural length exceeds XLEN bits (GCLEN saturates to XLEN, so the software-calculated top underflows).
security_spec.summary: GCTOP replaces the saturating-add top computation; kernel must use exactly one method per capability instance or risk divergent bounds that let a sandboxed compartment access memory beyond its intended top.

findings.finding: No Zytopr extension code exists in this kernel tree. Searched for ytopr, Zytopr, GCTOP, GCBASE, GCLEN (case-insensitive) across the entire tree — zero matches. The RISCV_ISA_EXT bitmap (arch/riscv/include/asm/hwcap.h) has no Zytopr entry. There is no capability bounds validation code, no saturating GCBASE+GCLEN addition, and no alternative-based switching between GCTOP instruction and software-calculated top. The vulnerability pattern (saturating GCBASE+GCLEN / using GCTOP on hardware lacking Zytopr, causing inconsistent top values when capability length exceeds XLEN bits) cannot be triggered because the code does not exist.
findings.snippet: // No Zytopr-related code found anywhere in the kernel tree

spec_citations.excerpt: Decode the top integer address from cs1's bounds, saturated to 2^MXLEN^-1, and write the result to rd.
Calculate the length of cs1's bounds ... defined as top - base. Return the maximum length, 2^MXLEN^-1, if the length of cs1 is 2^MXLEN^.
The base is XLEN bits and is inclusive. The top is (XLEN+1)-bits and is exclusive. The length is (XLEN+1)-bits and is defined to be top - base.
